elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted (a): "HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates" — express defence duty extending to affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)" in favour of the Company and its affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (i): "an allegation that the Site, the Services or any deliverable provided by HDI infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (iii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of the Company's data or Confidential Information caused by HDI".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (iv): "HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: (b): "The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of any such claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: (b): "the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: (b): "the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense of the claim".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: (c): Company indemnity runs only "to the extent arising out of the Content provided by the Company or the Company's breach of applicable law" — no broader Company indemnity for HDI's services.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same limb (i) IP infringement/misappropriation indemnity in favour of the Company.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification exclusion is included, which is more favourable to Customer than the fallback allows; condition therefore does not bite.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination carve-out inserted; the omission is Customer-favourable and does not defeat the level.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-specification carve-out inserted; nothing to satisfy.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause contains no procure/modify/replace remedy ladder for the infringing Site, Services or deliverable.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic appears in the inserted language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No monetary super-cap is stated; the Agreement also has no liability cap or annual-fee construct (payments are a share of Net Sales).

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements appear in the inserted Indemnification clause, including the affiliate-extended defence duty, all four indemnity triggers, the notice/control/cooperation procedure, and a Company indemnity narrowed to Company-provided Content and Company breach of law.

Fallback level is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund fallback, no 3x annual fees super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met; the drafter's reasoning that a 3x 'annual fees' cap is unworkable in a Net Sales revenue-share deal is sound.

Minimal: the edit is a single insertion of a previously missing clause placed between Section 9 and Section 10; the retained Globix carve-out and warranty text are untouched, and there are no extras such as survival tails, at-own-expense language, added damages categories or boilerplate. Extending limb (iii) to Confidential Information as well as Company data is within the data-breach element rather than a new requirement.

Preserves intent: no cap, remedy, timing or allocation provision is contradicted, and no existing cross-reference is disturbed; the Agreement previously had no indemnity or limitation of liability, so nothing conflicts.

Drafting nit for repair (not an element failure): limb (i) uses capitalised "the Services", which is not among the resolved definitions. Either lowercase it ("the services provided by HDI") or cite the Section 1 services description so the insertion leaves no arguably undefined capitalised term.
